clue.text: Queen Anne finally bit hazel nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange themselves
finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A queen nibbling hazelnuts, the last of them finally eaten by Queen Anne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Anne' looks like one royal, but Queen alone is the definition and Anne only lends its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth is the name of two English and British queens regnant, so it is an example of a queen.

clue.text: Old Testament female, New Testament incident

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A Bible student contrasts a woman from the Old Testament with an incident from the New.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a happening or occurrence, the same thing as an incident.

parts.note: something in fashion right now is 'in'
Diana is the Roman goddess of hunting

explanation.surface: A goddess figure is in vogue across a whole state just now.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty states of the USA, so it is an instance of a state.

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow, lying across them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone tearfully turns their back on the person who saved their life.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert is to turn aside or away, as in averting one's eyes or gaze.

clue.text: A street in dire need in part of London

indicators.note: in places the opening words inside the scrambled word that follows
dire suggests something in a terrible state, so the word after it is jumbled

parts.note: St is the usual abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A deprived street in a poor district of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditionally working-class area of London east of the City.
explanation.definitionFit: The East End is a district of the British capital, so it is literally a part of London.

clue.text: Shapely sort of figure for an old timer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a curvy body with a narrow waist
second meaning: a sand-filled device once used to measure time

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old timer' reads as a veteran person, but here it is literally an old device for timing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a waisted body shape and the two-bulbed sand glass that measures a set period.

clue.text: Change the course of a revolution

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to steer in a new direction
second meaning: one rotation, as of a wheel

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like altering history's direction through an uprising, but revolution here is a spin.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to redirect; as a noun it is a single rotation about an axis.

clue.text: Newly promoted male avoided underwater missile

indicators.note: newly suggests the letters are made afresh in a fresh order
avoided means the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man who has just been promoted dodges a missile fired from beneath the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: Take M out of PROMOTED, leaving PROOTED, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled weapon that travels under the sea's surface to its target.

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Eric is house-hunting for somewhere new to live.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is a home or dwelling place, a formal synonym of abode.

indicators.note: start to points to the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Pointless compass needles that begin to whirl round for no reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless describes something not required, the same sense as unnecessary.

indicators.note: seen after tells us the first item comes later in the order than the second

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Student writing published after a campus uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: To uprise is an old word for rising up in revolt, so its past tense means rebelled.

clue.text: Jacket's back on reference book, after much delay

indicators.note: on means one piece is placed next to and after the other

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A book cover's back jacket being finally fixed to a reference volume after a long wait.
explanation.definitionFit: At last is an idiom used when something finally happens following a long wait.

clue.text: Boffins, for example, with good leaders

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Clever scientists, say, together with fine people in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Boffin is British slang for a scientist or brainy expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggheads is informal for highly intellectual people, the same type as boffins.

indicators.note: taken part says only a portion of the run of words is used

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the third

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled that a rascal joined in.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means filled with horror or shock, matching horrified.

clue.text: Huge drink for mouse avoiding extremes

indicators.note: avoiding the extremes means leaving off the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A massive tipple poured for a little mouse that keeps away from the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: The trimming applies across both words 'for mouse', not mouse alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginormous is a jokey blend of gigantic and enormous, meaning extremely big.

explanation.surface: A drunk realises he is in a tricky predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight spot is an idiom for a difficult or dangerous predicament.

indicators.note: devouring means swallowing something so that it ends up inside

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Fire-breathing beasts eating up elderly cavalrymen.
explanation.definitionFit: Dragoons were soldiers who rode horses, originally mounted infantry.

clue.text: Grand eel, when wriggling, became bigger

indicators.note: something wriggling twists about, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A splendid eel swells up as it squirms.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlarged, the past tense of enlarge, means grew in size.

indicators.note: chopped means cut up, so the letters are broken and put back differently

explanation.surface: Corpses hacked about, playing on the idiom 'chopped and changed'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopped and changed' is a set phrase, but it splits into indicator and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Amended means altered or revised, usually to correct or improve.

clue.text: Play outside church with old Greek coin

indicators.note: outside places the first word around the second

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A play staged outside a church features an ancient Greek coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The drachma was the currency of Greece in antiquity and again until the euro.

indicators.note: in places the selected letter inside the following word
a starter is what comes first, so the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: An ideal first course in a wonderful dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' tempts as a course of the meal, but it only picks a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is an evening meal, so it is a kind of meal.

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A school play put on for every class.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform is to play, as a musician performs or plays a piece.

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters have gone wrong and are out of order

explanation.surface: A wholesome beverage prescribed for a teenager who misbehaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke that a healthy brew might reform a delinquent.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is an unfermented tea, a type of hot beverage.

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A church district that heats up the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is the local district served by one church and its priest.

explanation.surface: A query about a cushion for the chaplain.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the informal military term for a chaplain or priest.

indicators.note: traps means catches and holds something inside

parts.note: Stan Laurel, the comedian of Laurel and Hardy

explanation.surface: A laurel bush that catches a demon.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurel suggests the plant, but it is the surname of comic Stan Laurel.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is the Devil, the chief evil spirit of Christian belief.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... in traffic or plans
second meaning: an armed robbery at gunpoint

explanation.walkthrough: Two bare nouns, each a meaning of the same hyphenated word.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a stoppage that causes waiting and a theft by threat of violence.

indicators.note: taken in means admitted inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Time spent in ghastly hidey-holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hideouts are hiding places, refuges where people go to withdraw, i.e. retreats.

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An American editor taken advantage of.
explanation.definitionFit: Used means taken unfair advantage of, as in feeling used by someone.

clue.text: Skilled hand and master at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A capable deckhand and the ship's master out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' and 'master at sea' suggest a ship's crew, but the definition is a skilled worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman is a skilled manual worker such as a plumber, which is what a skilled hand means.
